issues.description: data.sh deduplicates utt_uttid and transcripts independently by sort -u, risking misalignment
issues.detail: The text file is built by pasting two separately sorted streams without a join on the utterance key. If either side has a duplicate or missing key (which the upstream pipeline does not guarantee absent), rows shift and utterances get the wrong transcript. The invariant 'row i of utt_uttid corresponds to row i of transcripts.txt' is unstated and unverified. Use join on the utt key instead of paste of two sorted streams.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is a fragile chain of sed substitutions with no documented character set
issues.detail: The pipeline strips one fullwidth A, one '#', '=', and a handful of Chinese punctuation, but the rationale and completeness are undocumented. Without a stated invariant ('text contains only characters in set S'), future inputs with sibling punctuation (e.g., '！', '：', '；', '（', '）') will silently survive into the vocabulary. State the target character class and assert it.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns but does not fail when unzip is missing or archives are absent
issues.detail: The unzip check echoes a message and continues; the missing-archive branches also echo and fall through, so the script can exit 0 with no data prepared, and data.sh proceeds to a confusing find with zero results. Either exit non-zero on missing prerequisites or have the caller verify the .complete sentinels. Termination-with-success on failure violates the script's contract.

issues.description: utt2spk uses the full filename as speaker ID, conflating recordings with speakers
issues.detail: TALASR<parent>-<file> as spk drops to the recording level, so spk2utt becomes one-utt-per-speaker for many partitions. Given the dataset advertises 80+ speakers with one speaker per utterance, this may be intentional, but the choice should be stated as a comment: 'we treat each recording session as a speaker because per-speaker labels are not provided.' Otherwise downstream speaker-aware tooling silently degrades.

issues.description: self_attention_dropout_rate: 0. and src_attention_dropout_rate: 0. are ambiguous YAML floats
issues.detail: YAML 1.1 parsers accept '0.' as float 0.0, but the trailing-dot form is non-portable and trips some strict parsers and linters. Write 0.0 for unambiguous numeric intent. Same nit applies to time_mask_width_ratio_range entries '0.' on line 84.

issues.description: README links and inline config path are inconsistent
issues.detail: The README references './conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml' in the rendered link target while the file actually lives at ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. A reader following the link gets a 404. Small, but literate-programming-grade documentation should resolve.

review.summary: The recipe is a conventional ESPnet egs2 bundle and the architecture/config files are reasonable. The principal rigor gap is in local/data.sh: the text file is assembled by paste of two independently sort -u'd streams, with no stated invariant that the rows align — a classic off-by-one waiting to happen if any utterance key drifts. The transcript normalization is an undocumented chain of sed substitutions over a partial Chinese-punctuation set; the target character class is not stated. download_and_untar.sh fails silently on missing tooling or archives. The YAML configs use trailing-dot floats (0.) which are non-portable. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED; the recipe likely works on the authors' machine but the invariants and failure modes are not literate.
